claims.text: On the evening of 15 October Dinis Cruz gave the first community talk at Agentic Engineering Live in London, after rUv's keynote, for the Agentics Foundation's London chapter.
claims.quote: I gave the first community talk at Agentic Engineering Live, after rUv's keynote

claims.text: The talk ran itself: twenty-six slides on a clock, most of them live web pages that animate themselves.
claims.quote: twenty-six slides on a clock, most of them live web pages that animate themselves

claims.text: The talk was built in about a day by a Ruflo hive of Claude Code subagents over nine runs, each with its own ephemeral sgit vault.
claims.quote: nine runs each with its own ephemeral sgit vault, and a ledger of every run

claims.text: The ledger of the runs records 28 workers and 57 vault commits, no plaintext in anything the server stored, every fresh clone identical, and every vault deleted at the end.
claims.quote: 28 workers, 57 vault commits, no plaintext found in anything the server stored

claims.text: In a separate proof of concept the same eleven actions went through Ruflo's policy engine in enforce mode and six were stopped, four denied and two sent to a person.
claims.quote: the same eleven actions went through Ruflo's policy engine in enforce mode and six were stopped

claims.text: The product is a hive, a memory and a mandate: Ruflo gives the many hands, an sgit vault gives the memory, and an Agent Behaviour Policy gives each role its mandate.
claims.quote: Ruflo gives the many hands; an sgit vault gives the memory, encrypted, versioned and kept by the client

claims.text: Agentics is the better word for what is sold, because it is the practice, not one workflow.
claims.quote: I think agentics is the better word for what we sell, because it is the practice, not one workflow.

claims.text: The market for agentic services is real and crowded at the top: the large consultancies have each built an agent platform, and the model vendors sell through partners and their own engineers.
claims.quote: The market for agentic services is real and crowded, and it is crowded at the top.

claims.text: Anthropic's Claude Partner Network, launched in March, committed an initial $100 million for 2026 and is open to any organisation bringing Claude to market.
claims.quote: an initial $100 million to this network for 2026

claims.text: OpenAI's consulting was reported in 2025 to start at about $10 million a client, delivered by forward-deployed engineers.
claims.quote: OpenAI's consulting was reported in 2025 to start at about $10 million a client

claims.text: rUv's company Cognitum sells consulting on the same stack, starting with a four-week discovery, then three months of deployment and a production term of one to three years.
claims.quote: starting with a four-week discovery, then three months of deployment and a production term of one to three years

claims.text: In London, Templab sells a one-week discovery audit for £2,500 and a two-week pilot agent from £8,000.
claims.quote: Templab sells a one-week discovery audit for £2,500 and a two-week pilot agent from £8,000.

claims.text: In Germany, Pragma-Code sells a 14-day AI sprint for €2,900, and AIGist24 sells a two-week assessment for $4,999.
claims.quote: Pragma-Code sells a 14-day AI sprint for €2,900.

claims.text: The boutique pattern is the same everywhere: a free call, a paid discovery, a fixed-price pilot, a build, a monthly retainer.
claims.quote: a free call, a paid discovery, a fixed-price pilot, a build, a monthly retainer.

claims.text: Gartner predicted in June 2025 that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027, citing escalating costs, unclear business value or inadequate risk controls.
claims.quote: Over 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by the end of 2027

value.unit: percent of agentic projects cancelled by end of 2027

claims.text: What the struggling organisations lack is not another platform but evidence: a run they can inspect, a record of what each agent did and was allowed to do, and output they keep.
claims.quote: Most offers in the market promise governance; few hand the client the record.

claims.text: The position is evidence first: every engagement leaves a vault the client keeps, with the work, the history, the ledger and a behaviour policy.
claims.quote: That is our position: evidence first. Every engagement leaves a vault the client keeps

claims.text: ruv.sgit.ai publishes four offers: task runs from £10 to £50, dedicated compute by the eight-hour block, a maintained repository from £149 a month, and expert time at £500, £1,500 and £5,000.
claims.quote: £5,000 for four days setting it up in the client's own environment

claims.text: A maintained repository of the whole setup is offered from £149 a month.
claims.quote: a maintained repository of the whole setup from £149 a month

claims.text: The engagement path is a free conversation, a first run for pounds, two hours or a day of expert time, a four-day pilot in the client's environment, then the maintained setup.
claims.quote: Each step is small enough to say yes to, and each ends with something they keep.

claims.text: There is no paid run yet, nothing automated end to end, and the pricing is a set of hypotheses to test with the first ten customers.
claims.quote: no paid run yet, nothing automated end to end

claims.text: Alongside the offers, a marketplace: a small curated list of consultants who deliver agentic engagements on this stack, where a client picks the project type first and then the people.
claims.quote: a small, curated list of consultants who deliver agentic engagements on this stack

claims.text: The first two consultants are Mondweep Chakravorty and Dinis Cruz; bookings are not open, so the page will say register interest, not book.
claims.quote: so for now the page will say register interest, not book.

claims.text: Consultants join by six steps copied from markets that work: apply, show proof of work, peer review, interview, a shadowed pilot, and standards including a behaviour policy for consultants.
claims.quote: The markets that work have converged on the same few steps, and we can copy them.

claims.text: Toptal publishes that fewer than 3% of applicants pass its five stages.
claims.quote: fewer than 3% of applicants pass its five stages

claims.text: For reference, Malt charges freelancers 5%, Upwork 0% to 15%, Braintrust a 15% fee to the client, and most markets sit between 5% and 20% in total.
claims.quote: Malt charges freelancers 5%, Upwork 0% to 15%, and Braintrust a 15% fee to the client

claims.text: The money, as a proposal: the consultant sets the price within the band and keeps most of it, and a small platform share pays for the catalogue, the runs and the vetting.
claims.quote: a small platform share pays for the catalogue, the runs and the vetting

claims.text: The brief for the marketplace page: one page on sgit.ai, the catalogue of five project types first, then one card per consultant, no checkout, the six steps published, and evidence on every card.
claims.quote: No checkout: register interest and book availability by email, until diaries are set.

claims.text: No paid engagement yet: the offers and prices are published, and nobody has bought one.
claims.quote: The offers and prices are published; nobody has bought one.

claims.text: The runs were not policy-gated; enforcement was shown in a separate proof of concept.
claims.quote: Enforcement was shown in a separate proof of concept.

claims.text: The market map is a judgement: positions are ours and prices are from public pages, and some market figures, Gartner's and OpenAI's, are from press releases and coverage.
claims.quote: Positions are ours; prices are from public pages.

claims.text: The marketplace is a design: nothing is built, and the platform share is a proposal.
claims.quote: Nothing is built; the platform share is a proposal.

claims.text: This is not rUv's or Cognitum's offer; it builds on their open-source stack.
claims.quote: It builds on their open-source stack.

claims.text: The article was written from a voice memo of 16 October 2026 by the site's agent, with the argument and editorial responsibility the owner's; readers who want to join write to agent@riskmandate.ai.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 16 October 2026, written by this site's agent in the voice of this site
